title: Ruovedentie 36 Säästökulman kiinteistön purku-urakka
description: Ruoveden kunta pyytää tarjousta omistamansa asuin- ja liikekiinteistö Säästökulman purku-urakasta tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaisesti. Purkukohde sijaitsee osoitteessa Ruovedentie 36, 34600 Ruovesi. Urakka sisältää rakennuksen purkamisen kokonaisuudessaan, purkujätteen asianmukaisen lajittelun, käsittelyn ja poiskuljetuksen sekä purkamisen jälkeiset maanrakennus-, täyttö- ja maisemointityöt. Kohteen sisätiloissa suoritetaan parhaillaan erillinen asbestipurku ja siihen liittyvä siivous laittoman haitta-ainepurun seurauksena. Suoritettavien töiden yhteydessä sisätiloista poistetaan tiedossa olevat asbesti- ja haitta-ainepitoiset materiaalit. Rakennuksen perustuksissa, julkisivuissa sekä muissa rakenteissa saattaa kuitenkin edelleen esiintyä haitta-aineita sisältäviä materiaaleja. Näiden materiaalien purkaminen, käsittely, pakkaaminen, kuljetus ja asianmukainen toimittaminen hyväksyttyyn vastaanottopaikkaan sisältyvät purku-urakkaan urakka-asiakirjoissa esitetyssä laajuudessa sekä voimassa olevien viranomaismääräysten mukaisesti. Tilaajalla on samanaikaisesti tarjouslaskennassa sisällöltään lähes vastaava purku-urakka. Kyseinen kohde sijaitsee noin 50 metrin etäisyydellä tästä purkukohteesta, ja kohteiden väliin jää yksi kiinteistö. Purkutyöt voidaan toteuttaa joko samanaikaisesti tai peräkkäin urakoitsijan tuotantosuunnittelun mukaisesti. Tarjoajaa pyydetään huomioimaan kyseinen mahdollinen synergiaetu tarjouslaskennassaan. Kohteet kilpailutetaan ja tilataan kuitenkin erillisinä toisistaan riippumattomina urakoina. Kumpaankin kohteeseen valitaan erikseen urakoitsija tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaisesti. Valintaperusteena on hinnaltaan halvin hyväksyt-tävä tarjous. Tarjouspyyntödokumentti, soveltuvuusvaatimukset, hankinnan kohde ja tarkemmat hankinnan tiedot tutustuttavissa latauslinkin takaa. Kohteeseen tutustuminen 7.12.2026 klo 9.00–10.00. Ilmoittautuminen esko.moisio@caverion.com, p. 050 347 8206 Urakkaan liittyvät kysymykset on toimitettava esko.moisio@caverion.com 9.12 mennessä. title: HAC6052 Integrated Adult Alcohol and Drug Prevention, Treatment and Recovery Service
description: This tender is for the recommission of the adult drug and alcohol treatment and recovery system through one integrated contract with a single accountable provider. The service will: • bring together core treatment, prescribing, psychosocial interventions, outreach, recovery support, IPS and agreed criminal-justice treatment/case-management functions; • provide a coherent resident pathway with strong harm-reduction, rough-sleeping, hospital, mental-health, primary-care, family, 18–25 and digital pathways; • retain formal interfaces with services outside the contract, including Reset Discovery (culturally sensitive recovery support service), P-RESET, Barts/ELFT, CYP provision, Tier 4 and Council-retained criminal-justice functions; • operate within a £7.37m annual financial envelope and commence on 25 October 2027. The Contract Period is initially for a period of three years, although the Authority reserves the right to extend the Contract on the same terms for further periods of 12 months, up to 24 months, making a total possible Contract Period of five years.

title: APN - Ramp B East Replacement Project 15 Wing, Moose Jaw, SK
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE Ramp B East Replacement Project 15 Wing, Moose Jaw, SK (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at 15 Wing Moose Jaw. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES CFB 15 Wing Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, requires the repair and replacement of the existing Ramp B East at the airbase.The Department of National Defence and Defence Construction Canada intends to put in place a contract to provide all labour, materials, and equipment for work including, but not necessarily limited to, the following:    Installation of temporary security fencing and construction barriers  Demolition and removal of existing concrete pavement  Partial removal of existing granular base  Topsoil stripping and stockpiling  Grading and compaction of the existing granular base and placement of new granular base  Construction of new Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) pavements  Installation of new joint sealant and paint markings  Landscaping, including topsoil, fertilizer, and hydroseeding  It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number: CN88327 Title: Ramp B East Replacement Project , 15 Wing, Moose Jaw, SK Approximate Estimate: $16,000,000 Anticipated Posting: January 2027 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a tenderer will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS) 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a tender for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential tenderers with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a tender.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit a tender will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the tenderer will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Wiley Reid Team Leader, Programs Defence Construction Canada 306-513-5681 Wiley.Reid@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the tenderer agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the tenderer for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

description: DLA Weapons Support - Richmond is issuing this source sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for the following: NSN 5977-00-311-6328 Sources: National Electrical Carbon (CAGE 0VJZ4) P/N 36A164453BCP01 The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 335991 THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, email address, Web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; 3) implement a successful project management plan that includes: compliance with tight program schedules; cost containment; meeting and tracking performance; hiring and retention of key personnel and risk mitigation; and 4) provide services under a performance based service acquisition contract. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION, and multiple awards MAY be made. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice by Dec 23, 2025 @ 2:00 pm EST. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice must be emailed to cassandra.cooper@dla.mil If you have any questions concerning this opportunity, please contact: Cassandra Cooper Email: cassandra.cooper@dla.mil APPENDIX 1: Purpose and Objectives Potential sources shall be capable of furnishing all labor, materials, facilities and equipment required to accomplish the new manufacture of the item(s). Generally, this entails the procurement/manufacture of component parts, inspection, testing, preservation/packaging, and shipping. Additionally, potential sources may be responsible for supply chain management, logistics planning, forecasting production requirements, long-lead time parts procurement, diminishing manufacturing sources and material shortage issues, and shipping serviceable assets. The unit prices will be established at the time of a contract award. Technical Orders and Qualification Requirements are not available.

This event will provide critical updates on the CNECTS requirement, featuring a comprehensive walk-through of the draft Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) and Area of Interest (AOI) document(s). Additionally, the Government will host virtual One-on-One meetings exclusively for new small business participants that have not had an opportunity to meet with the CNECTS acquisition team to ensure maximum opportunity for emerging partners to discuss their capabilities for he CNECTS requirements. 2. EVENT DATES & DETAILS Virtual Industry Day: Wednesday, 19 August 2026 Format: Virtual Only (MS Teams) Audience: Open to all interested industry partners. Key Focus: Detailed walk-through and Q&A session regarding the CNECTS draft CSO and AOI. Small Business One-on-One Meetings: Thursday, 20 August 2026 & Friday, 21 August 2026 Format: Virtual Only (MS Teams) Eligibility Requirement (CRITICAL): These sessions are strictly reserved for new small business participants that have not previously met with the CNECTS acquisition team. If your company has already engaged in a One-on-One for this requirement, please do not request a slot for these dates. Space is highly limited and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis for eligible firms. 3. ONE-ON-ONE REGISTRATION (OPEN NOW) ? Eligible small businesses may begin requesting their 1-on-1 time slots immediately. Space is highly limited and slots will be assigned on a first-come, first-served basis. How to Request: Email the Point of Contact listed below. Required Email Subject Line: CNECTS 1-on-1 Request - [Your Company Name] Information to Include in Request: Company Name & Unique Entity ID (UEI) Primary Point of Contact (Name, Email, Phone) Small Business and/or Socioeconomic Category (e.g., SDVOSB, WOSB, 8(a), HUBZone), if applicable Confirmation Statement: "We confirm that our company has not previously held a One-on-One meeting with the CNECTS acquisition team." 4. NEXT STEPS FOR THE VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY For general attendance at the Virtual Industry Day on August 19 (which does not require a 1-on-1 slot), formal MS Teams dial-in links and draft CSO/AOI materials will be posted here in the coming weeks. No registration is required for the main briefings on August 19. 5. POINTS OF CONTACT Submit your One-on-One meeting requests directly to: Primary POC: Rosalind Davis, Contracting Officer � rosalind.davis.3@spaceforce.mi 14 July 2026 Updated: Important Notice to Industry: Immediate Suspension of CMMC Phase II Requirements On behalf of the SAIO Acquisition Team, we want to ensure all industry partners are aware of a major policy announcement issued today by the Department of War (DoW) Chief Information Officer (CIO) and the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment. Effective immediately, the Department has suspended the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Phase II requirements, which were originally scheduled to go into effect on November 10, 2026. What does this mean? While Phase II is suspended to reduce administrative barriers, the Department maintains a strict cybersecurity posture: Phase I Remains Active: All CMMC Phase I self-assessment requirements remain firmly in place. Contractual Enforcement Continues: Contractual enforcement of cybersecurity remains fully active. All defense contractors must still comply with DFARS 252.204-7012, which requires the implementation of NIST SP 800-171 security controls to protect Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). 9 July 2026 Updated: General Status Updated Regarding the Acquisition Path and Timeline We appreciate your continued interest and your patience as we work through the pre-acquisition phases. This correspondence is to provide a general status update regarding the acquisition path and timeline: Current Review Status: The CNECTS follow-on is a highly complex acquisition that consolidates multiple legacy contracts across critical Space Force installations. At this time, several critical reviews and strategy documents have not yet been approved. Path Forward: Because of the technical and structural complexity of this effort, we are working diligently to secure all necessary senior-level approvals. As soon as we obtain a more definitive pathway and approved strategy, we will provide an updated milestone schedule to Industry. A Viable Requirement: We want to emphasize that this remains a highly viable contract action. The Government is fully committed to this consolidated effort and is actively progressing through the required regulatory steps. Virtual Industry Day: Due to the extensive delay between the initial Industry Day and the upcoming release of the CSO/Area of Interest (AOI), the Space Acquisition and Integration Office (SAIO) plans to host a Virtual-Only Industry Day. The purpose of this event will be to walk through the CSO and the specific AOI requirements prior to their release, aiming to address as many questions as possible before the official solicitation goes live. One-on-One Meetings: In conjunction with these updates, one-on-one (1-1) meetings will be offered to any new requesters that have not previously met with the CNECTS acquisition team. Due to high interest and resource constraints, we are unable to accommodate repeat meetings with previously engaged parties. As a reminder, when the solicitation is released, it will be executed as a 100% Small Business Set-Aside using the Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) phased evaluation process. We encourage you to continue to monitor SAM.gov for all future updates, draft releases, and formal announcements regarding this requirement. Thank you again for your time, interest, and continued support of this mission. 10 June 2026 Updated: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Decision At this time, the acquisition strategy has not been approved. Unfortunately, this process has taken longer than initially anticipated, and the Government is still actively working through the approval process. However, we are able to share an update regarding the SBA's decision: The SBA has officially released the two previous contracts�WICS II and PEDS�from the 8(a) program. Concurrently, the initially approved consolidated Justification and Approval (J&A) decision has been changed. Therefore, the CNECTS acquisition will now be competed as a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. Thank you all for your continued interest in the CNECTS acquisition. We appreciate your patience as we finalize the remaining acquisition strategy approvals. title: RFI - Novel or Multifunctional Fibers, Yarns, Coatings/Finishes and Fabrics for Soldier Protection and Comfort (MFFYF)
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army DEVCOM Soldier Center, in coordination with the Product Manager for Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE), to identify potential sources of multifunctional fibers, yarns, fabrics, coatings, or finishes for Soldier protection, thermal comfort and/or physical comfort. The RFI is issued for the purpose of identifying and assessing novel fibers, yarns, fabrics, coatings or finishes. Of primary interest are multifunctional submissions that provide at least two (2) functionalities (e.g., a moisture management fiber knit into a vector protective structure, an oil repellant coating or finish applied to flame resistant fabric). The Government seeks both near- and far-term approaches: Near-Term Solutions (TRL 5�7+): Mature, drop-in, or near-term standalone textile solutions that can be rapidly validated by DEVCOM SC and could be inserted into active military Programs of Record (PORs). Near-term solutions should be able to withstand laundering and abrasion while maintaining functionality. Far-Term Next-Generation Concepts (TRL 2�4): Emerging, exploratory concepts (e.g., novel fiber cross-sections, grooved/star-shaped capillaries, re-entrant geometries, mechanical vector-barrier architectures, vector protective chemistries, biomimetic moisture channels, and advanced microclimate finishes) to inform technology investments for future uniform platforms. The RFI is issued solely for information gathering and planning purposes. The RFI does not constitute a formal solicitation for proposals and will not directly lead to any contract awards. The following sections of this announcement contain details of the scope of technical interest as well as instructions for submitting a response. The Government requests that responses be submitted electronically to paola.a.dangelo.civ@army.mil and joseph.a.orlando38.civ@army.mil by 23 December 2026 by 5pm EST. Background: This RFI is intended to identify products and suppliers that provide textile multifunctionality to enhance the environmental protection of dismounted Warfighters. Dismounted Warfighters are often exposed to rapid shifts between extreme physical exertion (producing high metabolic sweat and vapor) and prolonged static postures (firing in the prone, kneeling on sub-zero surfaces, sitting in observation posts/foxholes). Protection against extreme environmental conditions (cold or hot, wet or dry) and the compounding physiological stresses induced by their specific mission profiles, equipment loads, and operational postures is desired. Description: Each material submission should ideally provide at least two (2) multifunctionalities that, when combined with other DEVCOM Soldier Center developments, have the potential of providing optimal protection for dismounted Warfighters operating in either temperate to cold or temperate to hot environments. While the primary interest of this RFI is in multifunctional solutions, the Government is also interested in novel, single-function materials in early stages of development (e.g., TRL 2-4) that demonstrate advancements in their respective performance areas. Submissions for single-function materials should include a description of their potential to be integrated with other materials (e.g., through coatings, fiber blends, or multi-layered systems) to create a multifunctional product in the future. These functionalities include but are not limited to: Moisture management: Approach features a moisture management solution that can transport liquid sweat rapidly to the outer face of the fabric and spread it across a large surface area. Evaporation directly against the skin in sub-freezing climates must be minimized to prevent cold related injuries. Must dry quickly in all temperature and humidity conditions. The movement of moisture out from trapped places is also of interest. Thermal protection: Approach must maintain uniform insulation value regardless of state (wet, dry, etc.). Solution must be lightweight and packable. Packing and unpacking should not impact level of insulation provided. Thermal Barrier: Solution/approach should be thin, lightweight, packable and have low thermal conductivity and should not be impacted by load or compression. Repellency: Outer layers must balance environmental protection with thermal and physiological management, categorized by the following distinct repellency performance tiers: Tier 1A: Aqueous Repellency (Water): Approach must repel liquid water (hydrophobicity) to prevent moisture saturation, and subsequent injuries. Tier 1B: Cryospheric Repellency (Ice): Approach must possess active ice-shedding properties to prevent ice buildup, moisture saturation, and subsequent cold-weather injuries. Tier 2: Organic Chemical Repellency: Approach should repel fuels (e.g., JP8), oils, and lubricants (oleophobicity). Vector protection: Approach should reduce the ability of the insect to find a blood meal (e.g., prevent landing and/or crawling, inhibit probing/feeding, block mouthpart penetration or other means of insect bite-through). Near-term approach must provide data that proves the functionality is durable after laundering and that air permeability and vapor transmission are maintained. Flame resistance (FR): All next-to-skin (N2S) near-term approaches (TRL 6+) must demonstrate superior flame resistance than defined in ASTM D6413 (char length ? 6.0 inches, after-flame ? 2.0 seconds) and exhibit no visible melting and dripping of polymer from the sample during testing. FR capability should not be affected by laundering. Far-term materials must also show promising heat release, heat capacity, arc flash and char yield performance. All approaches utilized to achieve these properties must be completely free of fluorinated compounds (PFAS-free). Respondents are welcome to submit militarily-relevant functionalities not listed here. Multifunctionalities can be an inherent component of the fiber, yarn, fabric construction, coatings or finishes and should be durable to laundering or abrasion. Near-term approaches (TRL 5-7+) that are submitted must meet DoD human-health toxicity and dermal contact safety requirements. Formulations must strictly avoid cyclic siloxanes (e.g., D4, D5, D6), silicones, and heavy metal catalysts. Specific Specifications and Deliverables: Respondents who are interested in responding to this announcement shall fill out the attached Appendix and provide: Company address, telephone number, primary contact(s) with email address(es). Business size, applicable NAICS code, CAGE code, and if you hold a GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract, your contract number. Explicit statement verifying whether the end product, intermediate processes, and raw precursor materials are 100% compliant with the Berry Amendment (10 U.S.C. � 4862) or will be in the future (and compliance target date is stated). Complete Global Harmonized System (GHS)-compliant Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) / Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all fibers, material components and chemicals included in each submission. Broad Construction Scope: Fabric submissions across all textile architectures�including wovens, knits (circular, warp and flat), nonwovens (including lofted insulation materials) felts, membranes, and hybrid composite constructions�are encouraged. A submission that displays at least two functionalities (e.g., moisture management and vector protection) is of higher interest. Architecture & Composition: Fiber generic type, cross-sectional morphology (round, star, multi-lobal), yarn linear density (denier/dtex), blend ratios/fiber content, areal weight (oz/yd2 or g/m2), yarn count, fabric construction, thickness and applied finishes. A fact sheet/white paper containing relevant standardized testing data/analysis that would indicate performance properties against the partial requirements listed above. title: Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004
description: ***This Amendment 001 is raised to modify the Challenge Stream - Call for Proposals 004 solicitation closing date.*** Introduction and Procurement Approach Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC) is issuing this Call for Proposals (CFP) on behalf of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada’s (ISED) Innovative Solutions Canada (ISC) program and participating departments, seeking to purchase innovative solutions to address a wide range of challenges facing federal departments and agencies. The purpose of this CFP is to create various pools of potential solutions that Canada may select from to address the challenges. Pools created as a result of this CFP can be utilized by any participating department. This CFP will be published on an ongoing basis for PWGSC to post departments’ challenges. Details related to each challenge, including entry phase, estimated number of contracts, maximum contract value, contract duration, the specific challenge closing date, and the essential and additional outcomes (if applicable) that the innovation must meet as long as it remains in the challenge stream, will be published under distinct Challenge Notices on the CanadaBuys website, which will form part of this CFP solicitation. 1.1 Innovative Solutions Canada Program Overview There are three components to the ISC program – the Challenge Stream, the Testing Stream and the Pathway to Commercialization. This CFP addresses entry and advancement through the Challenge Stream whereby solutions may later have the option of exiting the Challenge Stream for advancement into the Testing Stream. It also addresses entry to the Pathway to Commercialization. The Challenge Stream is designed to support the development of pre-commercial innovations by Small Businesses, with possible progression along a Technology Readiness (TRL) maturity scale. Entry into the Challenge Stream may occur at Phase 1 or at Phase 2, as specified in the individual Challenge Notices. Solutions may progress from entry TRL to a level which can be used by departments to solve the specific Challenge and be used in government operations. Challenge notices will specify the phases for which proposals can be submitted as set out in section 1.2.1. 1.2.1 Challenge Stream Entry 1.2.1.1 Entry at Phase 1: Proof of Feasibility Offerors with an innovation at TRL 1-4 may apply to enter the program at Phase 1. The objective of Phase 1 is for selected Offerors to conduct research and development (R&D) on their proposed solutions and deliver a proof of feasibility to Canada. Offerors are encouraged to progress their solutions as far as possible on the TRL scale during Phase 1. Offerors that demonstrate feasibility of their solution to the satisfaction of the sponsoring department upon completion of Phase 1 may be invited to submit a proposal for the Phase 2 outlined in section 1.2.2.1. Advancement to Phase 2 is not guaranteed. It is at the sole discretion of Canada to proceed with Phase 2. OR 1.2.1.2 Entry at Phase 2: Prototype Development Offerors with an innovation at TRL 5-9 may apply to enter directly into Phase 2, if specified in the Challenge Notice. The objective of Phase 2 is to conduct R&D on the proposed solution with the goal of developing, testing and delivering a prototype to Canada addressing the Challenge. Offerors enter into Phase 2 at TRL 5 to 9. Offerors are encouraged to progress their solutions as far as possible on the TRL scale during Phase 2. 1.2.2 Advancement of Research and Development Activities 1.2.2.1 Invitation to Advance to Phase 2: Prototype Development The objective of Phase 2 is to continue the R&D efforts of the proposed solution from Phase 1 with the goal of developing, testing and delivering a prototype to Canada for the selected Challenge. Small Businesses that have completed their Phase 1 contract and where the innovation remains of interest to Canada may receive an invitation, by way of a request for documentation, to advance to Phase 2 at the sole discretion of Canada. There is no minimum TRL level for a Phase 1 innovation to advance to Phase 2. Small businesses should not have any expectations of being invited to advance to Phase 2. In other words, there is no guarantee of participation in Phase 2. Canada will not provide justifications to small businesses as to why an innovation was not selected to participate in Phase 2. 1.2.2.2 Advancement into Testing Stream: Prototype Testing The objective of the Testing Stream is to procure, test and evaluate R&D pre-commercial goods and services in late-stage development (TRL 7 to 9), as defined on the ISC website here - https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/101.nsf/eng/00077.html. Canada may purchase multiple quantities of prototypes, test them and provide valuable feedback. In some cases, departments that originally sponsored the challenge may decide not to move forward with further research and development, however, small businesses may be matched with another Government of Canada Organization under the Testing Stream. Small businesses should not have any expectations of being offered the opportunity to submit a proposal. In other words, there is no guarantee of participation in Testing Stream: Prototype Testing. Canada will not provide justifications to Suppliers as to why an innovation was not selected to submit a proposal for Testing Stream: Prototype Testing. 1.2.2.3 Pathway to Commercialization The Pathway to Commercialization (PTC) component is an opportunity for companies that have a market-ready innovation developed under the ISC program to sell that innovation to the Government of Canada. The PTC includes a list that departments may consult as options to meet their requirements. Eligible Small Businesses who demonstrate successful completion of a Phase 2 or Testing Stream Contract may be eligible to submit a proposal for the Pathway to Commercialization. To be placed on the PTC List, Eligible Small Businesses will be required to, demonstrate how their innovation continues to meet their respective ISC requirements and provide a realistic commercialization plan. Should a Offeror qualify, the Small Business certification will be thoroughly re-validated prior to the contract award process. The innovation inclusion onto the PTC List will remain active for a period of up to three years after notice of qualification. Canada has no obligation to procure from this list and will determine the procurement strategy for each potential contract. Who Can Submit a Proposal for Challenge Stream Entry Offerors must certify program eligibility as part of their proposal. Selected Offerors must also re-certify eligibility before contract award. Re-certification may be required at any phase under the ISC program. Eligibility criteria must be met, or contracts may be terminated if a business fails to meet eligibility criteria during the contract period. Offerors must meet all the following eligibility criteria: for profit incorporated in Canada (federally or provincially) 499 or fewer full-time equivalent (FTE) employees* research and development activities that take place in Canada 50% or more of its annual wages, salaries and fees are currently paid to employees and contractors who spend the majority of their time working in Canada* 50% or more of its FTE employees have Canada as their ordinary place of work* 50% or more of its senior executives (Vice President and above) have Canada as their principal residence* * Calculations must consider and include affiliated businesses, such as parent companies and subsidiaries that are either in or outside of Canada. title: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Mission Training Complex (MTC)
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. This synopsis is hereby issued in accordance with FAR Part 5.203, to announce the Government's intent to award a 8-month, Firm Fixed-Price Bridge Contract, on a noncompetitive basis to Trideum Corporation (CAGE 351S9) for the Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Mission Training Complex Capabilities Support (MTCCS) effort. This is a notice of intent to award a sole source contract under statutory authority 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(l) set forth in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement Procedures, Guidance, and Information 206-302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Army Contracting Command-Orlando (ACC-ORL} and JBSA have identified a need to award a sole source contract to Trideum Corp (CAGE 351S9), to continue performance of JBSA MTCCS requirements. The current JBSA MTCCS Task Order expires 28 JAN 26. The contemplated sole source contract will include a limited performance period of five (5) months, commencing 29 JAN 2026 - 30 SEP 2026, ensuring continuation of mission command (MC) training at the JBSA Mission Training Complexes (MTCs). Services performed under this sole source contract will include the continuation of non-personal services to support the Mission Training Complex (MTC) to units stationed at and supported by Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA). No other contractor is in the position to assemble a large team of administrative, program management and subject matter experts (SMEs) who specialize in providing individual through collective Mission Command (MC} training, by the expiration of the current JBSA MTCCS contract performance period (28 JAN 26}. Award to anyone other than the incumbent contractor (Trideum) would result in a significant break in service. Award of this limited Bridge Contract is result of decrements identified in the Program Objective Memorandum for Fiscal Years FY27 through FY31 (POM 27-31), and as a result, the JBSA MTC will close at the end of FY26. This is NOT a request for competitive quotes. The Government intends to negotiate solely under statutory authority 10 U.S.C. 2304(c}(l) set forth in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1. Any interested firms must identity their interest and capability to respond to the requirement no later than 15 business days after this notice posts. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Please respond by 24 DEC 2025 at 1300 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST). Your response must include your stated technical knowledge of and experience with mission command (MC) training and information to demonstrate the Contractor's ability to complete Phase-In activities and commence full performance by the end of the current JBSA contract (28 JAN 2026). Send your response to Will Bass via willie.c.bass2.civ@army.mil. All responding contractors must be registered to the System for Award Management (SAM).

This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, email address, Web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. title: INDUSTRY DAY: WPC Work Platforms
description: INDUSTRY DAY: Department of Homeland Security, United States Coast Guard (USCG), Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC), CG Yard Location: USCG Yard, 2401 Hawkins Point Rd, Baltimore MD 21226 Description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an Industry Day event on 08 January 2026 at 9:00am ET. All interested parties are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view the registration information, attachments, and details below. The USCG plans to conduct a multi-phased approach to market research including: 1) requesting submission of capabilities statement, 2) an in-person industry day, and 3) one-on-one engagements with industry. The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) will be holding an Industry Day event to engage with industry about the USCG�s needs relating to a potential upcoming requirement(s) and obtain information from industry as the USCG continues to seek a system of work platforms to facilitate exterior hull preservation on the 154� WPC Fast Response Cutter. The USCG will share more information about the scope of the requirements, the challenges we have identified, and the goals of the program. The venue has a capacity limitation; therefore, each vendor is limited to two participants. To participate, vendors should email Linda.B.Lassiter@uscg.mil (Contract Specialist). All responses are due no later than 26 December 2025 at 4:00pm EST. The in-person Industry Day presentation will be recorded and or transcribed and publicly posted.? This is a follow-on to the USCG�s previously published Request for Information (RFI) that preliminarily describes the USCG�s needs. The previously published RFI (70Z04026RFI62204Y00) is attached to this Special Notice for reference purposes. INDUSTRY DAY AND ONE-ON-ONE SESSIONS GENERAL Industry Day The USCG will host an Industry Day on 08 January 2026, from 9:00am � 11:30am ET. A finalized agenda for the event will be sent out by 02 January 2026. In preparation for the in-person Industry Day, USCG asks interested vendors to review the information provided in the appendices and submit questions to Linda.B.Lassiter@uscg.mil (Contract Specialist), so the USCG can be prepared to share the questions received and the answers. Please be advised that all questions and answers will be shared publicly. Therefore, interested parties are encouraged not to submit proprietary information with their questions. One-on-One Sessions The one-on-one engagements with vendors will occur immediately following the in-person industry day on 08 January 2026. Vendors should express their interest in a one-on-one session when registering via email. The USCG will follow up, no later than 02 January 2026, with a scheduled time for one-on-one engagements. There will be approximately 8 time slots available for one-on-one sessions. Each appointment is limited to approximately 15 minutes. Your confirmed one-on-one time will be included as a follow-on email to your registration confirmation. The purpose of these one-on-one sessions is to gather objective feedback, foster open dialogue, and obtain information from industry as the USCG continues to seek a system of work platforms to facilitate exterior hull preservation on the 154� WPC Fast Response Cutter. [YA1] [LL2] This will provide interested vendors with an opportunity to share potential proprietary solutions/services information for consideration and allow the Government to ask the vendor specific questions. These sessions are not a platform for vendor promotion. NOTE: Please be advised that if your company has already submitted questions regarding the requirements in response to our previous Request for Information (RFI), these questions will be addressed on SAM.gov, with select questions discussed during the Industry Day. All questions will be answered by the date the Industry Day recording is posted. Registration If your company plans on attending the General Session of the Industry Day and/or scheduling an appointment for a One-on-One session, please email Linda.B.Lassiter@uscg.mil (Contract Specialist) no later than 26 December 2025 at 4:00pm EST. If requesting to schedule an appointment for a one-on-one session, please be sure to request it at this time. The Government will follow up no later than 02 January 2026 with a scheduled time for one-on-one engagements. Proposed Schedule of Events. 9:00am ET to 11:30am ET: Industry Day, Briefings on Scope of Requirements, Challenges and Goals. 11:30am ET to 12:30pm ET: Lunch 12:30pm ET to 3:00pm ET: One-on-One�s - Approximately 8 time slots available for one-on-one sessions. Each appointment is limited to approximately 15 minutes (Subject to change based on responses) Attachments: USCG Special Announcement-Industry Day WPC Work Platforms List of Prohibited Items Request for Information (RFI): 70Z04026RFI62204Y00 Accessing Federal Facilities: Starting on May 7, 2025, all adults 18 and older will need to present REAL ID compliant state-issued identification or other acceptable ID to enter USCG Yard. Under the direction of building owners, the Federal Protective Service will ensure that all entrants meet the necessary entry requirements. Upon arrival, individuals may be asked to present a REAL ID-compliant driver�s license, passport, or other acceptable ID (https://www.tsa.gov/travel/securityscreening/identification). This change is designed to enhance security while establishing consistent identification standards across federal facilities nationwide. Questions Regarding This Special Notice: For questions regarding this Special Notice regarding the upcoming Industry Day and One-on-One Sessions, please send them to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist listed below. description: ATVIRAS PROJEKTO KONKURSAS. Tauralaukio rajono teritorijos, pagal Klaipėdos miesto bendrojo plano sprendinius patenkančios į 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.8 ir 9.9 nagrinėjamus rajonus, urbanistinės idėjos atviras projekto konkursas. Projekto konkurso tikslas - išrinkti geriausiai urbanistinius, architektūros ir funkcinius aspektus bei kitus reikalavimus, išvardintus konkurso sąlygose, atitinkančią Tauralaukio rajono teritorijos, pagal Klaipėdos miesto bendrojo plano sprendinius patenkančios į 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.8 ir 9.9 nagrinėjamus rajonus, urbanistinės idėjos projektą, kurio pagrindu ateityje bus rengiami teritorijų planavimo dokumentai ir vystoma ši Tauralaukio rajono teritorija. Biudžetas: šio projekto konkurso pirkimo objekto įgyvendinimui (t.y. urbanistinės koncepcijos parengimui) suplanuota suma - 50 000 Eur su PVM (41 322,31 Eur be PVM). Vadovaujantis VPĮ 55 str. 3 d. Perkančioji organizacija konkurso dokumentuose iš anksto nustato fiksuotą kainą projekto konkurso pirkimo objekto įgyvendinimui (t.y. urbanistinės koncepcijos parengimui) - 50 000 Eur su PVM (arba 41 322,31 Eur be PVM, jei tiekėjas yra ne PVM mokėtojas ar paslaugos neapmokestinamos PVM, ar dėl kitų priežasčių, dėl kurių Perkančiosios organizacijos galutinė tiekėjui mokėtina suma bus be PVM). Projekto konkurso pirmąsias 3 vietas užėmusius dalyvius numatyta apdovanoti piniginiais prizais (premijomis), skiriant 40 000 Eur, prizinį fondą išskirstant tokia seka: I vieta – 16 000 Eur; II vieta – 14 000 Eur; III vieta – 10 000 Eur. Perkančioji organizacija laimėjusiu nustato tik 1 (vieną) dalyvį, surinkusį daugiausiai balų ir esantį pirmoje vietoje, neatitikusį pašalinimo pagrindų ir atitikusį nustatytus kvalifikacijos reikalavimus. Su projekto konkurso laimėtoju numatoma sudaryti paslaugų pirkimo–pardavimo sutartį dėl urbanistinės koncepcijos parengimo.

The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. title: ECP 6315C3 Navigation Warfare NAVWAR A-Kits for F/A-18E/F Aircraft
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of the F/A-18 and EA-18G Program Office (PMA-265), intends to award a firm-fixed price (FFP) delivery order against existing sole-source Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N00019261002 to the Boeing Company. This procurement is for the manufacturing, assembly and installation support of Engineering Change Proposal (ECP) 6315C3 Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR) A-Kits in FY27, supporting both United States Navy (USN) and Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) F/A-18 and EA-18G aircraft configurations. The anticipated period of performance anticipated will commence in December 2026 and expected to span approximately 17 months. Boeing is the designer, developer, manufacturer, and integrator of the F/A-18 aircraft in its various configurations; and as such, is the only known firm with the knowledge, experience, and technical expertise required to accomplish this effort. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS AND NO COMPETITIVE SOLICITATION WILL BE ISSUED. This synopsis is for informational purposes only. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole source basis under the authority permitting other than full and open competition is Title 10, U.S. Code 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.103-1, �Only one responsible source and no other supplies or series will satisfy agency requirements�. There is no commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation, make an award or awards, or be responsible for any money expended by interested parties before award of a contract for the effort described above. Information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit or award a contract. Subcontracting opportunities should be sought directly from The Boeing Company Small Business Liaison Officer, Taylor Beitler, taylor.beitler@boeing.com.

title: NATO Business Opportunity: Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) Tactical Battle Management (TBM) Capabilities
description: The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) intends to issue a solicitation for the provision of a Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) Tactical Battle Management (TBM) System including In-Service Support and Enhancements. Potential U.S. prime contractors must 1) maintain a professionally active facility (office, factory, laboratory, etc.) within the United States, 2) hold a Facility Security Clearance (FCL) at the level of SECRET or higher, 3) be pre-approved for participation in NATO Competitive Procurement (NCP), 4) be issued a Declaration of Eligibility (DOE) by the Department of Commerce (DOC), and 5) register with NCIA�s eProcurement tool, Neo: https://www.ncia.nato.int/business/procurement/neo-eprocurement Pre-competitive Industry Engagement will take place in the form of a BMD TBM Workshop at NATO Edge, taking place on 17-19 November in Izmir, T�rkiye. Please see the attached Calling Notice for details. More information on NATO Edge attendance and registration is available on event�s official website -https://www.natoedge.nato.int/. For those who cannot attend NATO Edge, a pre-competitive Request for Information is included in the second attachment. Submit responses via the email address in the attachment no later than 12:00 hours Central European Time (CET) on 03 December 2026. The reference for the solicitation is CCO-423316-RTBMD and all correspondence concerning the solicitation should include this reference. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT Please see attached. BECOMING ELIGIBLE TO BID NCP requires that the U.S. Government issue a DOE for potential U.S. prime contractors interested in this project. Before the U.S. Government can do so, however, the U.S. Government must approve the U.S. firm for participation in NCP. U.S. firms are approved for NCP on a facility-by-facility basis. The U.S. NCP application is a one-time application. The application requires supporting documentation in the form of 1) a company resume or capability statement indicating contracts completed as a prime contractor and 2) an annual report or set of financial documents indicating compilation, review, or audit by an independent CPA. The U.S. Government continues to accept the legacy NATO International Competitive Bidding (ICB) application for participation in NCP. U.S. firms can download a copy of the legacy ICB application from the following website: https://www.bis.gov/about-bis/bis-leadership-and-offices/SIES/business-opportunities-nato DOC is the U.S. Government agency that approves NCP applications. Please submit to the email address provided your application and supporting documentation (as attachments). If your firm is interested in a specific NCP project at this time, please also include the following in the TEXT of your email: - the title and/or solicitation number of the project - the name/phone/email of the company employee who should receive the bid documents After approval of your one-time NCP application, DOC will then know to follow up by issuing a DOE for the project. DOC will transmit the DOE to the NATO contracting agency. title: Solicitation for a Concessions Business Opportunity to provide Kayak Rental Services within Glacier Bay National Park
description: The National Park Service (NPS) provides notice of the release of a Prospectus to solicit proposals for the award of a Concession Contract (No. CC-GLBA035-27) to provide kayak rental services within Glacier Bay National Park & Preserve. The effective date of the next Concession Contract is expected to be February 1, 2027. The Prospectus explains the business opportunity and the terms and conditions under which the NPS will award the Concession Contract. The Prospectus will be available at the link below. Offerors' Site Visit The NPS will not host a site visit in association with this solicitation. Interested offerors are encouraged to visit Glacier Bay National Park to familiarize themselves with the area. Questions Due If you do not understand something in this Prospectus, you must submit your questions or comments via email to AKRO_Concessions@nps.gov no later than 4:00 p.m. Alaska Standard Time on October 21, 2026. The questions must be in a format that allows the NPS to copy them to Microsoft Word. Notice of Intent to Propose If you plan to submit a proposal in response to this solicitation, you must notify the Service via email at AKRO_Concessions@nps.gov no later than 4:00 p.m. Alaksa Standard Time on October 28, 2026. The NPS will not accept proposals from entities that do not provide notice on or before that date. Submission of an electronic proposal In order to be evaluated and considered for award of a Concession Contract, the Electronic Proposal must be received by the Service no later than 4:00 p.m. Alaska Standard Time on December 28, 2026. After the Notice of Intent to Propose deadline and prior to the electronic proposal submission deadline, you will receive a welcome email message from the Service's Microsoft Teams platform at the email address you provided when you notified the Service of your intent to submit a proposal. You must accept the invitation before you can access the Teams site to upload your proposal. The Service will not accept proposals submitted in hardcopy or via another electronic platform, including email. See Prospectus Part II Proposal Instructions for details on submitting an Electronic Proposal. Contact List To be put on a contact list to receive amendments or any additional information specific to the Prospectus, interested parties must provide their contact information (name, email address, and phone number) to the Service via email at AKRO_Concessions@nps.gov. Information relative to the solicitation will also be posted to the above-mentioned website. The contact list already includes the Existing Concessioner. Summary of Due Dates: Questions Due: October 21, 2026 Notice of Intent to Propose Due: October 28, 2026 Electronic Proposals Due: December 28, 2026 Hardcopy Offeror's Transmittal Letter Due: January 4, 2027

description: Platform One, with support from its marketplace manager, The Applied Research Institute (ARI), is initiating a long-term, open call for solutions to support the DoD in quickly delivering high-quality, secure software with accelerated delivery times. The solutions will support or enable the delivery of resilient software capability at the speed of relevance, ensuring the DoD remains agile and responsive to emerging threats and opportunities. Specifically, Platform One seeks to obtain innovative solutions or potential capabilities that fulfill requirements, close capability gaps, or provide potential technological advancements. Innovative solutions encompass technologies, processes, or methods (including research and development) that are newly developed or applied in a novel way as of the submission date. This initiative, entitled the �Platform One Solutions Marketplace� (P1SM) will solicit, collect, assess, and curate hardware, software, or service solutions and make those solutions available through rapid acquisition pathways. This approach aims to foster innovation and expedite the integration of cutting-edge technologies into the DoD's operational framework, enhancing its ability to deliver software at the speed of relevance.

Germany – Flocculating agents – Klärwerk Koblenz_Rahmenvertrag Flockierungsmittel
description: Gegenstand der Ausschreibung ist die Lieferung und Dienstleistung von Flockungsmittel für das Klärwerk Koblenz. Die Kläranlage Koblenz behandelt hauptsächlich kommunales Abwasser. Laut Bescheid hat sie eine Ausbaugröße von 320.000 EW. Mit einem Einwohnerwert von rund 154.000 EW (in 2022) behandelt sie jedoch weniger Fracht als ursprünglich vorgesehen. 126.000 Einwohner sind reell angeschlossen (Einwohnerzahl EZ). Die restlichen 28.000 Einwohnergleichwerte (EWG) sind industriellen Ursprungs (EZ+EWG=EW). Damit ergibt sich ein Industrieanteil des zu behandelnden Abwassers von rund 18%. Haupteinleiter sind die Papierindustrie, das Metallgewerbe und eine Mälzerei. Die maschinelle Faulschlammentwässerung erfolgt mit zwei Dekantern (X4E-4/454, BJ 2023). Die Entwässerung soll mit bestmöglichem Austrags TR bei optimalem Polymerbrauch durchgeführt werden. Der Abscheidegrad liegt bei > 98% (gem. DWA M-383); das Zentrat wird zurück zur Kläranlage geleitet. Für die Eindickung und Entwässerung wird ein Emulsionspolymer eingesetzt. Der anfallende Überschussschlamm wird mit drei Zentrifugen (GEA UCD 346 BJ 2012) unter Einsatz von Emulsionspolymeren maschinell eingedickt.

De dienstverlening die ingekocht wordt is bedoeld voor schoolteams van scholen voor (speciaal) basisonderwijs (po), speciaal onderwijs, voortgezet (speciaal) onderwijs, gevestigd op Amsterdams grondgebied. En voor rijksbekostigd middelbaar beroepsonderwijs gevestigd op Amsterdams grondgebied. De Gemeente beoogt met het gunnen van deze opdracht aan diverse Opdrachtnemers te bewerkstelligen dat Amsterdamse schoolteams (bestaande uit docenten, onderwijsondersteunend personeel, directie etc.) gezamenlijk worden getraind in omgaan met en pedagogisch handelen bij ernstig grensoverschrijdend gedrag van kinderen en jongeren in en om school. Op die manier ondersteunt de Gemeente de Deelnemers bij het realiseren van een veilig schoolklimaat. In deze Leidraad is de gedetailleerde omschrijving van de Opdracht en de daaraan gestelde eisen opgenomen.

title: AFCENT Battle Lab Commercial Solutions Opening
description: Please Note: While SAM.gov displays a specific Inactive Date, this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) is continuously open. Solution Briefs will be accepted and evaluated on a rolling basis at any point prior to the listed Inactive Date. Further, listed PSC and NAICS are placeholder only, final PSC and NAICS will be determined at time of propsal/award. Shaw AFB, South Carolina is conducting a CSO authorized by 10 U.S.C. 3458 and R-DFARS 212.70 and its associated class deviations. Under a CSO, the Air Force may competitively award proposals received in response to a general solicitation to acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, and services. Under this CSO, all items, technologies, and services shall be treated as commercial items. Awards will be RFO Part 12 contracts. The Air Force intends to obtain "innovative" solutions or potential new capabilities that fulfill requirements, close capability gaps, or provide potential technology advancements. Solutions may include existing technologies or procedures, not currently in use by the Air Force, that would enhance or streamline Air Force mission capabilities. �Innovative� is defined as any technology, process or method that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal. It also includes any new application of an existing technology, process, or method. The Government is not obligated to make any awards, and all awards under this CSO are explicitly subject to the availability of funds and successful negotiations. The Government is not responsible for any monies expended by any vendor prior to the issuance of any awarded contract. The Government reserves the right to modify the solicitation requirements of this CSO at its sole discretion. The Government seeks to deploy rapid, commercial off-the-shelf counter-UAS capabilities; fuse advanced intelligence and multi-source data to create a comprehensive operational picture; develop innovative kinetic and non-kinetic solutions to defeat coordinated UAS swarms; leverage agile software and rapid prototyping methodologies; implement modular open-systems approaches (MOSA) for seamless sensor integration; and establish sustainable, open-standard architectures to drive continuous competition. This enables the Department of War (DoW) to continuously field adaptable, integrated, and resilient defensive capabilities against rapidly evolving aerial and multi-domain threats. The CSO is a streamlined acquisition process that seeks to reduce acquisition timelines and acquire new, innovative solutions that vendors can bring forth to meet the stated Areas of Interest. Performers may need to demonstrate the capability to work in classified environments up to the Secret level before any award, if necessary. While this CSO is primarily designed to fulfill the requirements of the Shaw AFB Battle Lab and United States Air Forces Central (AFCENT), it may be leveraged to support broader Department of the Air Force (DAF) or Department of War (DoW) requirements under strict execution guidelines. To maintain oversight and prevent misuse, this CSO is not authorized for decentralized use by outside contracting offices. All external requirements must be validated and routed directly through AFCENT, and the 20th Contracting Squadron will retain sole procurement authority for all contract awards. Shaw AFB is focused on rapidly acquiring and deploying counter-UAS (cUAS) and defensive capabilities that form a cohesive, enterprise-wide open architecture ecosystem. The following focus areas are representative examples of the capabilities of interest; however, this is not an exhaustive list. The Government is open to, and highly encourages, innovative solutions from industry that address other technologies or approaches that align with the strategic vision outlined below. Solutions that address technologies across multiple pillars are encouraged. Teaming and Partnership for Turnkey Solutions: To mitigate the risks of disjointed systems and reduce administrative burden, the Government highly encourages industry vendors to form strategic partnerships, joint ventures, or Prime/Subcontractor teaming arrangements to submit complete, end-to-end solutions. Proposals that offer a single lead system integrator managing a suite of best-of-breed commercial technologies are strongly preferred over submissions for isolated, piecemeal components. The intent is to streamline the acquisition, delivery, and sustainment process by fielding cohesive, fully integrated systems. The Government seeks commercial capabilities that provide end-to-end defensive solutions, from immediate point defense to advanced data integration and long-term capability sustainment. Vendors may provide insight on solutions that address all or some of the capability pillars below. The desired end-state is a deployable capability that effectively counters evolving aerial threats while exploiting open architecture principles across its full lifecycle (development, integration, test, deployment, operations, and sustainment). An ideal partner has a first-party ability to directly leverage underlying commercial technologies to meet operational requirements; supporting partners would be considered enabling providers for specific aspects of the potential solution.

description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Sacramento District (SPK), issues this Presolicitation Notice (Synopsis) for a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Environmental Remediation Services (ERS) ACQUISITION STRATEGY and SCOPE Acquisition Type: Unrestricted with a Small Business Reserve. Both large and small business concerns are encouraged to submit proposals. Target Pool Size: Approximately seven (7) Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. Reserve Allocation: The Government intends to reserve four (4) to six (6) awards exclusively for qualified Small Business concerns, and one (1) to three (3) awards for Unrestricted (Large Business) firms. The Government reserves the right to award fewer. Evaluation Method: Subjective Best Value Tradeoff process in accordance with FAR Part 15 and DoD Source Selection Procedures. Program Ceiling: $230.5 Million over a 5.5-year ordering period. Scope: Broad ERS activities including Hazardous, Toxic, and Radioactive Waste (HTRW) remediation, Military Munitions Response Program (MMRP) actions, and emerging contaminant cleanup (e.g., PFAS). CONCURRENT SEED PROJECT This solicitation features a concurrent, funded seed task order award: Project Name: Carrington Island Precision Bombing Range Munitions Response Site, FUDS No. J08UT077701.Scope of Work: Investigation, excavation, and remediation of munitions and debris. Labor Standards: This is a hybrid construction and service action incorporating both Wage Rate Requirements (Construction/Davis-Bacon Act [DBA]) (Heavy Construction) and Service Contract Labor Standards (SCA).Award: The responsible Offeror providing the best overall value for the Carrington Island seed project will be awarded the initial firm-fixed-price task order concurrently with their basic MATOC contract. Remaining pool awardees will receive a basic contract with a minimum guarantee of $2,500.00. SOLICITATION DETAILS Anticipated RFP Release Date: On or about November 20, 2026.Access: The solicitation will be issued solely through the PIEE Solicitation Module (https://piee.eb.mil). Offerors must have an active SAM registration (https://sam.gov) and have the Proposal Manager role activated in PIEE to view and submit proposals. title: AFCENT Battle Lab Commercial Solutions Opening
description: Please Note: While SAM.gov displays a specific Inactive Date, this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) is continuously open. Solution Briefs will be accepted and evaluated on a rolling basis at any point prior to the listed Inactive Date. Further, listed PSC and NAICS are placeholder only, final PSC and NAICS will be determined at time of propsal/award. Shaw AFB, South Carolina is conducting a CSO authorized by 10 U.S.C. 3458 and R-DFARS 212.70 and its associated class deviations. Under a CSO, the Air Force may competitively award proposals received in response to a general solicitation to acquire innovative commercial items, technologies, and services. Under this CSO, all items, technologies, and services shall be treated as commercial items. Awards will be RFO Part 12 contracts. The Air Force intends to obtain "innovative" solutions or potential new capabilities that fulfill requirements, close capability gaps, or provide potential technology advancements. Solutions may include existing technologies or procedures, not currently in use by the Air Force, that would enhance or streamline Air Force mission capabilities. �Innovative� is defined as any technology, process or method that is new as of the date of submission of a proposal. It also includes any new application of an existing technology, process, or method. The Government is not obligated to make any awards, and all awards under this CSO are explicitly subject to the availability of funds and successful negotiations. The Government is not responsible for any monies expended by any vendor prior to the issuance of any awarded contract. The Government reserves the right to modify the solicitation requirements of this CSO at its sole discretion. The Government seeks to deploy rapid, commercial off-the-shelf counter-UAS capabilities; fuse advanced intelligence and multi-source data to create a comprehensive operational picture; develop innovative kinetic and non-kinetic solutions to defeat coordinated UAS swarms; leverage agile software and rapid prototyping methodologies; implement modular open-systems approaches (MOSA) for seamless sensor integration; and establish sustainable, open-standard architectures to drive continuous competition. This enables the Department of War (DoW) to continuously field adaptable, integrated, and resilient defensive capabilities against rapidly evolving aerial and multi-domain threats. The CSO is a streamlined acquisition process that seeks to reduce acquisition timelines and acquire new, innovative solutions that vendors can bring forth to meet the stated Areas of Interest. Performers may need to demonstrate the capability to work in classified environments up to the Secret level before any award, if necessary. While this CSO is primarily designed to fulfill the requirements of the Shaw AFB Battle Lab and United States Air Forces Central (AFCENT), it may be leveraged to support broader Department of the Air Force (DAF) or Department of War (DoW) requirements under strict execution guidelines. To maintain oversight and prevent misuse, this CSO is not authorized for decentralized use by outside contracting offices. All external requirements must be validated and routed directly through AFCENT, and the 20th Contracting Squadron will retain sole procurement authority for all contract awards. Shaw AFB is focused on rapidly acquiring and deploying counter-UAS (cUAS) and defensive capabilities that form a cohesive, enterprise-wide open architecture ecosystem. The following focus areas are representative examples of the capabilities of interest; however, this is not an exhaustive list. The Government is open to, and highly encourages, innovative solutions from industry that address other technologies or approaches that align with the strategic vision outlined below. Solutions that address technologies across multiple pillars are encouraged. Teaming and Partnership for Turnkey Solutions: To mitigate the risks of disjointed systems and reduce administrative burden, the Government highly encourages industry vendors to form strategic partnerships, joint ventures, or Prime/Subcontractor teaming arrangements to submit complete, end-to-end solutions. Proposals that offer a single lead system integrator managing a suite of best-of-breed commercial technologies are strongly preferred over submissions for isolated, piecemeal components. The intent is to streamline the acquisition, delivery, and sustainment process by fielding cohesive, fully integrated systems. The Government seeks commercial capabilities that provide end-to-end defensive solutions, from immediate point defense to advanced data integration and long-term capability sustainment. Vendors may provide insight on solutions that address all or some of the capability pillars below. The desired end-state is a deployable capability that effectively counters evolving aerial threats while exploiting open architecture principles across its full lifecycle (development, integration, test, deployment, operations, and sustainment). An ideal partner has a first-party ability to directly leverage underlying commercial technologies to meet operational requirements; supporting partners would be considered enabling providers for specific aspects of the potential solution.

description: 1. Zakup autobusów zeroemisyjnych dla ZKM Zawiercie sp. z o.o. w ilości 3 szt. 2. Szczegółowy opis przedmiotu zamówienia (OPZ) zawiera załącznik nr 1a do SWZ. 3. Zakres zamówienia obejmuje dostawę ww. autobusów wraz z wyposażeniem, niezbędnym oprogramowaniem, dokumentacją i przeprowadzeniem szkoleń na warunkach określonych w niniejszej specyfikacji warunków zamówienia. 4. Wymagania dotyczące spełniania przepisów: 1) Oferowany autobus musi spełniać wymagania i warunki określone w Regulaminie nr 107 Europejskiej Komisji Gospodarczej Organizacji Narodów Zjednoczonych (EKG ONZ) - Jednolite przepisy dotyczące homologacji pojazdów kategorii M2 lub M3 w odniesieniu do ich budowy ogólnej [2015/922] (Dz.U.UE.L.2015.153.1 z dnia 2015.06.18), zwanego dalej Regulaminem nr 107 EKG ONZ. 2) Oferowane autobusy musi być wyposażony w silnik/silniki elektryczne. 3) Oferowany autobus musi być wykonany przy maksymalnym wykorzystaniu materiałów niepalnych, szczególnie w zakresie materiałów użytych do konstrukcji i wyposażenia wnętrza nadwozia oraz posiadać homologację EWG pojazdu odnośnie do palności z badań niepalności elementów wyposażenia przedziału pasażerskiego oraz kabiny kierowcy wykonanych zgodnie z Regulaminem nr 107 Europejskiej Komisji Gospodarczej Narodów Zjednoczonych (EKG ONZ). 4) Oferowany autobus musi spełniać wymagania określone w przepisach zawartych w Dziale III ustawy z dnia 20 czerwca 1997 r. – Prawo o ruchu drogowym (Dz.U. z 2017 r., poz. 1260 z późn. zm.) oraz odpowiadać warunkom technicznym określonym w rozporządzeniu Ministra Infrastruktury z dnia 31 grudnia 2002 r. w sprawie warunków technicznych pojazdów oraz zakresu ich niezbędnego wyposażenia ( tekst jedn. Dz.U. z 2016, poz. 2022). 5) Oferowany autobus musi spełniać wymagania i warunki określone w Rozporządzeniu Ministra Infrastruktury z dnia 25 marca 2013 r., w sprawie homologacji typu pojazdów samochodowych i przyczep oraz ich przedmiotów wyposażenia lub części (Dz.U.2015.1475 z dnia 2015.09.25, z późniejszymi zmianami). 6) Oferowany autobus musi spełniać normę PN-S-47010:1999 lub równoważna dla autobusu miejskiego klasy I lub M . 7) Autobus musi spełniać wymagania określone w Rozporządzeniu Ministra Infrastruktury z dnia 31grudnia 2002 r. w sprawie warunków technicznych pojazdów oraz zakresu ich niezbędnego wyposażenia (Dz.U. z 05 marca 2015r., poz. 305). 8) Oferowany typ autobusu musi posiadać aktualne Świadectwa Homologacji Typu Pojazdu lub Świadectwo Zgodności WE Typu Pojazdu – w rozumieniu ustawy z dnia 20 czerwca 1997 roku Prawo o ruchu drogowym (tekst jednolity Dz.U. z 2017 poz. 1260) lub świadectwo krajowego indywidualnego dopuszczenia pojazdu wydane przez Dyrektora Transportowego Dozoru Technicznego, stanowiące podstawę do jego zarejestrowania na terenie Polski. Wykonawca dostarczy w/w dokument najpóźniej w dniu realizacji dostawy. 9) Dostarczany autobus w dniu podpisania protokołu zdawczo-odbiorczego musi odpowiadać aktualnym przepisom rejestracji pojazdów i musi posiadać niezbędne dokumenty dopuszczające do sprzedaży i rejestracji pojazdów Wydziale Komunikacji Starostwa Powiatowego. 10) Autobus ma być dostarczony do siedziby Zakładu Komunikacji Miejskiej Zawiercie, ul. Polska 21 wraz z dokumentacją naprawczą i obsługową, licencjami oprogramowań niezbędnymi do obsługi zakupionego autobusu, tj.: a) karty gwarancji pojazdów, b) książki gwarancyjne, c) książki serwisowe (przeglądów). 11) W sytuacji, gdy w okresie między złożeniem przez Wykonawcę oferty w postępowaniu o udzielenie zamówienia, a realizacją umowy nastąpi zmiana przepisów prawa w zakresie rejestracji, homologacji, sprzedaży lub wprowadzenia do użytku nowych autobusów (a także zespołów i podzespołów do tych autobusów), Wykonawca zobowiązany jest zrealizować przedmiot zamówienia z uwzględnieniem tychże zmian. 12) Oferowany autobus nie może być prototypem oraz musi być fabrycznie nowy, to znaczy wyprodukowany nie wcześniej niż 9 miesięcy przed terminem dostawy, nieużywane do celów prezentacyjnych, testowych i podobnych, nierejestrowane, z przebiegiem nie większym niż 2000 km. Autobus stanowiące przedmiot zamówienia musi: a) być dostosowany do potrzeb wszystkich użytkowników, w tym być dostępne dla osób niepełnosprawnych zgodnie z opisanymi wymaganiami technicznymi, b) tabor autobusowy będzie uwzględniać wymogi i dobre praktyki określone w Załączniku nr 2. Standardy dostępności dla polityki spójności 2021-2027 w Wytycznych dotyczących realizacji zasad równościowych w ramach funduszy unijnych na lata 2021-2027; c) zakupiony tabor będzie uwzględniał kwestie bezpieczeństwa, w szczególności na rzecz niezmotoryzowanych uczestników ruchu (w tym kobiet). W taborze zostaną zastosowane rozwiązania wspomagające kierowcę w ochronie pieszych i rowerzystów (w tym kobiet), np. systemy ostrzegania o kolizji; d) rozwiązania wynikające ze standardu GSR2 - system monitorowania ciśnienia i temperatury w oponach , - asystent skrętu w prawo , -asystent pasa środkowego , -system monitorowania zachowania kierowcy, - aktywny tempomat sprzężony z układem hamulcowym , oraz inne systemy bezpieczeństwa autobusu wymagane przepisami w momencie rejestracji pojazdu . cd w sekcji informacje dodatkowe

title: Armed Protective Security Officer Services, Los Angeles Area
description: Armed Protective Security Officer (PSO) Services, Los Angeles Area The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Protective Service (FPS) has a requirement to acquire armed Protective Security Officer (PSO) services throughout Los Angeles, CA and surrounding areas.
